And if her 'iddah passes without his taking her back, she becomes a matter for a suitor (khitab), and this is what Allah commanded, and this is the divorce of the Sunnah. As for one who divorces at every menstruation, he has erred from the Sunnah, disobeyed the Lord, and taken hardship upon himself.

⁕ Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out﴾: He said: He divorces according to the Sunnah and returns according to the Sunnah. He claimed that a man among the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, called 'Awf al-Ashja'i, had a son, and the polytheists took him captive, and he was among them. His father used to come to the Prophet ﷺ and complain to him about his son's whereabouts, his condition, and his need. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would command him to be patient and say to him: "Allah will surely make a way out for him." He did not wait long after that before his son escaped from the hands of the enemy. He passed by a flock of the enemy's sheep and drove them off, and brought them to his father, and he came with them with wealth he had obtained from the sheep. So this verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from ʿAmmar ibn Abi Muʿawiya al-Duhni, from Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd, regarding ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Ashja' tribe who came to the Prophet (ﷺ) in distress, and he asked him for help. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Fear Allah and be patient." He said: "I have done so." So he went back to his people, and they said: "What did he say to you?" He said: "He said: 'Fear Allah and be patient.'" They said: "I said: 'I have done so,' until he said that three times." So he returned and found his son, who had been a captive among the Banu so-and-so of the Arabs, and he came with some goats. He then went back to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "My son was a captive among the Banu so-and-so, and he has come with some goats. Are they lawful for us?" He said: "Yes."

He said: ʿAmmar al-Duhni related to us, from Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd, concerning His saying: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Ashja' tribe who was afflicted with hardship, so he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and he said to him: "Fear Allah and be patient." He returned and found that his son, who had been a captive, had been freed by Allah from their hands, and he had acquired some goats. He came and mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Are they lawful for me, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes."

He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn al-Mundhir al-Thawri, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym, regarding ﴿He will make for him a way out﴾. He said: From every matter that becomes narrow for people.

He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, regarding ﴿He will make for him a way out﴾. He said: He knows that Allah, if He wills, withholds from him, and if He wills, gives to him. ﴿And provides for him from where he does not expect﴾: that is, from where he does not know.

He said: Mihran related to us, from Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArouba, from Qatada, regarding ﴿He will make for him a way out﴾. He said: From the doubtful matters and the anguish at death. ﴿And provides for him from where he does not expect﴾: from where he does not hope or anticipate.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And provides for him from where he does not expect﴾: he does not anticipate or hope.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾.

He, may He be exalted, means: whoever fears Allah in his affairs and entrusts them to Him, then He is sufficient for him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾.

This is a separate statement from His saying: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾. Its meaning is: Indeed, Allah accomplishes His command in every case, whether the servant relies upon Him or does not rely upon Him.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) also said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, regarding ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾: He is sufficient for him whether he relies upon Him or does not, except that the one who relies upon Him will have his misdeeds expiated and will be given a great reward.

Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, saying: Abu Muʿawiya related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, with something similar.

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Silt related to us, from Qays, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud), regarding ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾. He said: The one whose need has been fulfilled is not the one who relies (upon Allah). The superiority of the one who relies upon Him over the one who does not is that his misdeeds are expiated and he is given a great reward.

He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: Shutayr ibn Shakl and Masruq were sitting together. Shutayr said: "Either you relate what you have heard from Ibn Masʿud so that I may confirm it, or I relate it so that you may confirm it for me?" Masruq said: "No, rather you relate it and I will confirm it." He said: "I heard Ibn Masʿud say: The greatest verse in the Qur'an regarding tafwid [[As in the original; I have not found this noun or its verb in the lexicons, and it is perhaps a corruption of "tafwid," which is the committing of the whole matter to Allah, and this is the meaning understood from this statement of Ibn Masʿud.]] is: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾." Masruq said: "You have spoken truly."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah has already set for everything a extent﴾.

He, may He be exalted, means: Allah has already set for everything, from divorce, the waiting period, and other matters, a limit, a term, and a measure at which it ends.

The people of ta'wil also said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Muʿawiya related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, regarding ﴿Allah has already set for everything a measure﴾. He said: A term.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, regarding ﴿Allah has already set for everything a measure﴾. He said: An endpoint.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, the same.

Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah has already set for everything a measure﴾. He said: The menstruation, in terms of the term and the waiting period.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 65, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 3)**

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period ('iddah, the prescribed waiting period after divorce), and count the waiting period. Fear God, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality. These are the limits of God, and whoever transgresses the limits of God has wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps God will bring about some matter after that.﴾ (1) ﴿Then when they have reached their term, either retain them in kindness or part from them in kindness, and call to witness two just men from among you, and establish the testimony for God. This is what is admonished to whoever believes in God and the Last Day. And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out (makhraj), (2) and will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon God, then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, God accomplishes His purpose. God has already set a decree for everything.﴾ (3)

He, exalted is His remembrance, means by His words ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾: when you divorce your wives, divorce them in their purity (tuhr) in which they count their waiting period, while they are pure without having had intercourse, and do not divorce them during their menstruation (hayd), which does not count as part of their waiting period (qur', the menstrual cycle, which in this context refers to the period of purity or the menstrual period, as the scholars differ).

The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said: I heard al-A'mash, from Malik ibn al-Harith, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), he said: "Divorce for the waiting period is in a state of purity without intercourse."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Malik ibn al-Harith, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Abdullah, regarding ﴿so divorce them for their waiting period﴾: "In a state of purity without intercourse."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim (al-Nakha'i), from Abdullah, regarding ﴿when you divorce women﴾, he said: "When you divorce, [it should be] in a state of purity without intercourse."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah, regarding ﴿so divorce them for their waiting period﴾: "In a state of purity without intercourse."

• Ibn Wakic narrated to us, he said: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Dawud ibn Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he considered the Sunnah divorce (talaq al-sunnah, the divorce prescribed by the Prophetic practice) to be in a state of purity without intercourse, and in every purity, and this is the waiting period that God commanded.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid, that a man asked Ibn Abbas and said: "I divorced my wife a hundred times." He said: "You have disobeyed your Lord, and your wife has been irrevocably separated from you, and you did not fear God, so He will not make a way out for you." And he recited this verse: ﴿And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out﴾, and he said: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the commencement of their waiting period﴾.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, with something similar.

• Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, he said: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid, who said: "I was with Ibn Abbas when a man came to him and said: 'I divorced my wife three times.' He remained silent until we thought he would return her to him. Then he said: 'One of you goes and rides the foolishness, then says: O Ibn Abbas, O Ibn Abbas! And God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out﴾, and you have not feared God, so I do not find a way out for you. You have disobeyed your Lord, and your wife has been irrevocably separated from you.'" God said: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the commencement of their waiting period﴾.

• Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, who said: "I heard Mujahid narrating from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾," and Ibn Abbas said: "At the commencement of their waiting period."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Umayya, from Abdullah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid, that he recited ﴿divorce them at the commencement of their waiting period﴾.

• al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Azim narrated to us, he said: Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, he said: Sufyan informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿so divorce them for their waiting period﴾, he said: "In a state of purity without intercourse."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Harun ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan (al-Basri), regarding His words ﴿so divorce them for their waiting period﴾, he said: "In a state of purity without menstruation, or pregnant whose pregnancy has become evident."

• Harun narrated to us, from Isa ibn Yazid ibn Dab, from Amr, from al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, regarding one who wishes to divorce three times all at once in a single utterance: that there is no harm in it, after he divorces her at the commencement of her waiting period, as God commanded him. But they both disliked that a man divorce his wife with one divorce, or two, or three, when it is not in the waiting period that God mentioned.

• Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: Awn informed us, from Ibn Sirin, that he said regarding His words ﴿so divorce them for their waiting period﴾: "He divorces her while she is pure without intercourse, or pregnant whose pregnancy is evident."

• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿so divorce them for their waiting period﴾, he said: "For their purity."

• Ali ibn Abd al-A'la al-Mihrabi narrated to us, he said: al-Mihrabi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding the saying of God ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾, he said: "The 'iddah is the qar' (menstrual cycle), and the qar' is the menstruation (hayd). And the tahir is the one who is pure without intercourse, then she waits through three menstrual periods."

• Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, Bishr said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾: "The waiting period is that he divorces her in a state of purity without intercourse with one divorce."

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿so divorce them for their waiting period﴾, he said: "When she has become pure from menstruation without intercourse." I said: "How?" He said: "When she is pure, divorce her before you touch her. If it seems to you that you should divorce her again, leave her until she menstruates once more, then divorce her when she becomes pure a second time. When you want to divorce her a third time, wait until she menstruates, then when she is pure divorce her a third time. Then she observes one menstrual period, and then she may marry if she wishes."

• Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, he said: Ibn Tawus said: "When you want to divorce, divorce her when she becomes pure, before you touch her, with one divorce. It is not proper for you to add to it until three cycles (qurū') have passed, for one divorce will make her irrevocably separated."

• It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿so divorce them for their waiting period﴾: "He divorces her while she is pure without intercourse."

• Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿so divorce them for their waiting period﴾: "When you divorce her for the waiting period, the power of her [divorce] is in your hand. Whoever divorces for the waiting period, God has made for him a latitude in that, and has given him the right to return her, if he wishes to take her back before the waiting period ends, he may take her back."

• Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾, he said: "In a state of purity without intercourse. If she does not menstruate, then at the beginning of every new moon."

• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: "I divorced my wife while she was menstruating." He said: "Umar came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to inform him of that, and he said: 'Command him to take her back, and let her remain until she becomes pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure again. Then if he wishes, let him divorce her before he has intercourse with her, and if he wishes, let him keep her. This is the waiting period that God, mighty and majestic, mentioned.'"

• He said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, with something similar, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

• Ibn Wakic narrated to us, he said: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, that "he divorced his wife while she was menstruating, so Umar asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'Command him to take her back, then let him keep her until she becomes pure, then she menstruates, then becomes pure again. Then if he wishes, let him keep her, for that is the waiting period in which God commanded women to be divorced.'"

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, "that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating, so Umar came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and he commanded him to take her back, then leave her until she becomes pure, then she menstruates, then he divorces her." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "That is the waiting period in which God commanded women to be divorced," and he said: "When they become pure."

• Ali narrated to us, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿so divorce them for their waiting period﴾, he said: "He should not divorce her while she is menstruating, nor in a state of purity in which he has had intercourse with her. Rather, he leaves her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then he divorces her with one divorce. If she menstruates, her waiting period is three menstrual periods, and if she does not menstruate, her waiting period is three months, and if she is pregnant, her waiting period is until she gives birth to her child."

• Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, he said: Amr ibn Abi Salama narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz, who was asked about the saying of God ﴿so divorce them for their waiting period﴾, and he said: "The Sunnah divorce is that a man divorces his wife while she is at the commencement of her waiting period, and she is pure without intercourse, with one divorce. Then he leaves her, and if he wishes, he takes her back before she bathes from the third menstruation. If he wishes to divorce her thrice, he divorces her with one divorce at the commencement of her waiting period, while she is pure without intercourse, then he leaves her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then he divorces her again. Then he leaves her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then he divorces her again, and then she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband."

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) regarding his divorce of Hafsa.

Those who said that:

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) divorced Hafsa bint Umar with one divorce, so this verse was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾. It was said: 'Take her back, for she is one who fasts much and prays much at night, and she is among your wives in Paradise.'"

* *

As for His words ﴿and count the waiting period﴾:

He means: and count this waiting period and its periods, and preserve them.

The scholars of interpretation have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

• Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿and count the waiting period﴾, he said: "Preserve the waiting period."

* *

As for His words ﴿Fear God, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses﴾:

He means: and fear God, O people, your Lord, so beware of disobeying Him by transgressing His limits. Do not expel those of your wives whom you have divorced for their waiting period from the houses in which you had lodged them before the divorce, until their waiting period ends.

The scholars of interpretation have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

• Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿Fear God, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses﴾, "until their waiting period ends."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Ibn Juraij informed us, he said: Ata' said: "If he permits her to observe the waiting period outside his house, and she observes it in her family's house, then he has shared with her in the sin." Then he recited: ﴿Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾. He said: "I said: Is this verse about this?" He said: "Yes."

• Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Hayawa ibn Shurayh informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, from Nafi', that Abdullah ibn Umar used to say regarding this verse ﴿Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾: "Her leaving before the end of the waiting period." Ibn Ajlan said, from Zayd ibn Aslam: "If she commits an immorality, she is expelled."

• Ali ibn Abd al-A'la al-Mihrabi narrated to us, he said: al-Mihrabi narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾, he said: "It is not permissible for her to leave except with his permission, and it is not permissible for the husband to expel her while she is in the waiting period. If she leaves, she has no right to lodging or maintenance."

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words (and fear God, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave): "She is the divorced woman who should not leave her house as long as her husband has the right of return (raj'a) over her, and she is in the waiting period."

• Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave﴾: "That is when he has divorced her once or twice, she has [the right to stay] as long as he has not divorced her three times."

* *

As for His words ﴿nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾:

The Exalted One means: Do not expel them, unless they commit a clear immorality, one that is recognized as immorality by whoever witnesses or knows of it.

The scholars of interpretation have differed regarding the meaning of the immorality mentioned in this passage, and the reason for which God permitted their expulsion from their houses while they are in the waiting period. Some of them said: The immorality mentioned here is adultery (zina), and the expulsion God permitted is expulsion for the enforcement of the prescribed punishment (hadd).

Those who said that:

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾, he said: "Adultery." He said: "So she is taken out in order that the prescribed punishment may be enforced upon her."

• Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, the like of it.

• Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Salih ibn Muslim, who said: "I asked Amir (al-Sha'bi): 'A man divorced his wife with one divorce; may he expel her from her house?' He said: 'If she is an adulteress.'"

• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾, he said: "Unless they commit adultery."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 65, verses 1–3 (part 2 of 3):

⁕ Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: I asked him about the words of Allah, mighty and majestic, ﴿Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾. He said: Allah, whose praise is great, said: ﴿And those of your women who commit immorality﴾. He said: These are the muhsanat (married women). ﴿Then call four witnesses from among you against them﴾ ... the verse. He said: So Allah made their prescribed punishment stoning. She should not leave her house, unless she commits a clear immorality; and if she commits a clear immorality, she is taken out to receive the hadd (prescribed penalty) and is stoned. Before this, the punishment for the married woman was confinement: she was kept in houses and not allowed to marry. For the two virgins (al-bikrayn), the punishment was harm. Allah, whose praise is great, said: ﴿And the two who commit it among you, harm them﴾, meaning: O adulterer, O adulteress. ﴿But if they repent and reform, leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾. He said: Then all of this was abrogated (naskh), and stoning became the punishment for the married man and woman, and one hundred lashes became the punishment for the virgins. He said: And this was abrogated.

Others said: The immorality which Allah meant in this place is bad conduct (al-badha') toward their in-laws.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said, regarding Allah's words: ﴿Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾: The clear immorality is that she behaves badly toward her family.

Others said: Rather, it is every disobedience to Allah.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾, and "immorality" means disobedience.

Others said: Rather, it refers to her nushuz (disobedience or ill-conduct) toward her husband, in which case he divorces her on account of that nushuz, and she then has the right to move out of her house.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾: Qatadah said: Unless he divorces her for nushuz, in which case she may move out of her husband's house.

Others said: The clear immorality which Allah, mighty and majestic, mentioned in this place is her going out of her house.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿and they should not leave unless they commit a clear immorality﴾: He said: Her going out of her house is an immorality. Some of them said: Her going out, if she commits an immorality, is that she goes out so that the hadd is carried out upon her.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi related to me, saying: Sa'id ibn al-Hakam ibn Abi Maryam related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan related to me, from Nafi', from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, regarding His words: ﴿Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾: He said: Her leaving before the end of the 'iddah (waiting period) is an immorality.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is the view of the one who said: By "immorality" in this place is meant disobedience. This is because immorality is every ugly matter in which a limit is transgressed: adultery is among it, and theft, and bad conduct toward in-laws, and her moving away from the dwelling in which she is obliged to observe the 'iddah. So whichever of these she does while she is in her 'iddah, her husband has the right to expel her from that house, because of the immorality she has committed.

* *

His words: ﴿And these are the limits of Allah﴾.

Allah, whose remembrance is great, says: These matters which I have explained to you concerning divorce for the 'iddah, the counting of the 'iddah, the command to fear Allah, and that the divorced woman should not leave her house unless she commits a clear immorality, are the limits of Allah which He has set for you, O people, so do not transgress them. ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged himself﴾. Allah, whose remembrance is great, says: Whoever goes beyond the limits of Allah which He has set for His creatures has wronged himself; that is, he has earned a burden for himself, and thereby becomes an oppressor toward himself and a transgressor against himself.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said the like of what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding Allah's words: ﴿And these are the limits of Allah﴾: He said: These are the obedience to Allah, so do not transgress them. He said: Whoever is other than this has wronged himself.

* *

His words: ﴿You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾.

Allah, whose praise is great, says: You do not know what will happen; perhaps Allah will bring about, after your divorcing them, a return (raj'ah).

The people of ta'wil have said the like of what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, that Fatimah bint Qays was married to Abu Hafs al-Makhzumi. The Prophet ﷺ had appointed 'Ali over part of Yemen, and he went out with him. [Abu Hafs] sent her a final divorce (tatliqah) that she had. He ordered 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah al-Makhzumi and al-Harith ibn Hisham to provide maintenance for her. They both said: "No, by Allah, she has no maintenance from us, unless she is pregnant." So she came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him. He did not assign her maintenance unless she was pregnant. She asked his permission to relocate, and she said: "Where should I move to, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "To the house of Ibn Umm Maktum," who was blind; she would take off her clothes in his presence and he would not see her. She remained there until the Prophet ﷺ married her to Usamah ibn Zayd when her 'iddah had ended. Then Marwan ibn al-Hakam sent for her to ask her about this report, and she informed him. Marwan said: "We have not heard this report except from a woman, and we will hold to the 'ismah (binding authority) which we found the people upon." Fatimah said: "Between me and you is the Book." Allah, whose praise is great, says: ﴿So divorce them for their 'iddah﴾, until [He reaches] His words: ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾. She said: "What matter will be brought about after three [divorces]? This is only about a man's returning to his wife. And how can a woman be detained without maintenance?"

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: He said: This is about a man's returning to his wife.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: That is, a return.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: He said: He may return to her in her house, in the case of one or two [divorces]; it is further away from adultery.

Sa'id said: al-Hasan said: This is in the case of one or two [divorces], and Allah does not bring about anything after three.

⁕ Ya'qub related to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ayyub informed us, saying: I heard al-Hasan and 'Ikrimah say: A woman divorced three times and a woman whose husband has died have neither residence (sukna) nor maintenance. He said: 'Ikrimah then said regarding ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: "What will happen after three [divorces]?"

⁕ 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-A'la al-Muharibi related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: He says: Perhaps the man will return to her during her 'iddah.

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: This is the case in which he has a right of return (raj'ah) over her.

⁕ Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: He said: The return.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: He said: Perhaps Allah will bring about in your heart a desire to return to your wife. He said: And whoever divorces for the 'iddah, Allah grants him latitude in that matter and gives him the power to take her back, so if he wishes to return before the 'iddah ends, he may do so.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: He said: Perhaps he will take her back.

* *

His words: ﴿Then when they reach their term﴾.

Allah, whose remembrance is great, says: When the divorced women who are in the 'iddah reach their term, that is, when the end of their waiting period draws near, ﴿then retain them in kindness﴾. He says: Then retain them by a return, if you wish to take them back, in kindness, that is, in accordance with what Allah has commanded you regarding retention, which is by giving them the rights that Allah has made obligatory upon him for them: maintenance, clothing, housing, and good companionship. Or ﴿part with them in kindness﴾, or leave them until their 'iddah ends, and they will be separated from you in kindness, meaning by giving her what right she has over him, such as the dowry and the consolatory gift (mut'ah), according to what he is obliged to give her.

The people of ta'wil have said the like of what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: al-Muharibi ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad related to me, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: ﴿Then when they reach their term﴾: He says: When her 'iddah ends before she has bathed from the third menstruation, or three months if she does not menstruate. He says: So return to her, if you wish to take her back, before her 'iddah ends, by retaining her in kindness, and kindness means to treat her well. ﴿Or part with them in kindness﴾. Parting in kindness means that he leaves her until her 'iddah ends, and gives her a dowry if she has one due from him upon divorcing her; that is parting in kindness, and the consolatory gift is according to one's means.

⁕ Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿Then when they reach their term﴾: He said: If he divorces her once or twice, [then] he may, as he wills, retain her in kindness or release her in kindness.

* *

His words: ﴿And call to witness two just men from among you﴾.

Call witnesses to the retention, if you retain them; that is the return. [Call] two just men from among you, meaning two whose religion and trustworthiness are satisfactory.

We have already explained earlier the meaning of "just" (al-'adl), in sufficient detail that it need not be repeated here, and we mentioned what the scholars said about it.

The people of ta'wil have said the like of what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: If he wishes to take her back before her 'iddah ends, he should call two men as witnesses, as Allah said: ﴿And call to witness two just men from among you﴾, at the time of the divorce and at the time of the return. If he takes her back, she is with him on the basis of two divorces. If he does not take her back, then when her 'iddah ends she is separated from him by one [divorce], and she is free to decide for herself, and then she may marry whomever she wishes, him or another.

⁕ Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿And call to witness two just men from among you﴾: He said: For the divorce and the return.

* *

His words: ﴿And establish testimony for Allah﴾.

He says: Bear witness for the truth when you are called upon to bear witness, and give it correctly when you are summoned to give it.

The people of ta'wil have said the like of what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿And establish testimony for Allah﴾: He said: Bear witness for the truth.

* *

His words: ﴿That is admonished thereby whoever should believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾.

Allah, whose remembrance is great, says: This which I have commanded you, and have made known to you regarding the matter of divorce, and what is obligatory for some of you toward others at parting or retention, is an admonition from Us to you, by which We admonish whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, so that he affirms it.

By His words ﴿whoever believes in Allah﴾ is meant whoever has the quality of faith in Allah, such as the one who:

⁕ Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿whoever should believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾: He said: believes in it.

* *

His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out﴾.

Allah, whose remembrance is great, says: Whoever fears Allah, acting upon what He has commanded him and avoiding what He has forbidden him, Allah will make for him a way out of his affair, by informing him that what Allah has decreed must come to pass. This is because when a man divorces, as Allah has enjoined upon him for the 'iddah, and does not take her back during her 'iddah until it ends, and then his soul pursues her, Allah makes for him a way out regarding what his soul pursues: He makes for him a path to proposing to her and marrying her. Whereas if he had divorced her three times, he would have had no path to that.

* *

His words: ﴿And will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾.

That is, He will cause the means of provision to reach him from where he does not perceive or know.

The people of ta'wil have said the like of what we have said on this matter, and some of them mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Salt related to us, from Qays, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah, regarding His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out﴾: He said: He knows that it is from Allah, and that Allah is the One who gives and withholds.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, regarding ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out﴾: He said: The way out is that he knows that Allah, blessed and exalted, if He wills, gives, and if He wills, withholds. ﴿And will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾: He said: From where he does not know.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, the like of it.

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out﴾: He says: His deliverance from every distress in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Rabi' ibn al-Mundhir, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, regarding ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out﴾: He said: From every matter that becomes straitened for people.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, from Yazid, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out﴾: He said: Whoever divorces as Allah commanded, Allah will make for him a way out.

⁕ 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-A'la al-Muharibi related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out﴾, and [He will make for him] ease in his affair. He said: By the way out and the ease is meant that if he divorces one [time] and then remains silent regarding her, he may, if he wishes, take her back with the testimony of two just men; that is the ease Allah spoke of. And if her 'iddah passes without his taking her back, she becomes a matter for a suitor (khitab), and this is what Allah commanded, and this is the divorce of the Sunnah. As for one who divorces at every menstruation, he has erred from the Sunnah, disobeyed the Lord, and taken hardship upon himself.

⁕ Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out﴾: He said: He divorces according to the Sunnah and returns according to the Sunnah. He claimed that a man among the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, called 'Awf al-Ashja'i, had a son, and the polytheists took him captive, and he was among them. His father used to come to the Prophet ﷺ and complain to him about his son's whereabouts, his condition, and his need. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would command him to be patient and say to him: "Allah will surely make a way out for him." He did not wait long after that before his son escaped from the hands of the enemy. He passed by a flock of the enemy's sheep and drove them off, and brought them to his father, and he came with them with wealth he had obtained from the sheep. So this verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from ʿAmmar ibn Abi Muʿawiya al-Duhni, from Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd, regarding ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Ashja' tribe who came to the Prophet (ﷺ) in distress, and he asked him for help. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Fear Allah and be patient." He said: "I have done so." So he went back to his people, and they said: "What did he say to you?" He said: "He said: 'Fear Allah and be patient.'" They said: "I said: 'I have done so,' until he said that three times." So he returned and found his son, who had been a captive among the Banu so-and-so of the Arabs, and he came with some goats. He then went back to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "My son was a captive among the Banu so-and-so, and he has come with some goats. Are they lawful for us?" He said: "Yes."

He said: ʿAmmar al-Duhni related to us, from Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd, concerning His saying: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Ashja' tribe who was afflicted with hardship, so he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and he said to him: "Fear Allah and be patient." He returned and found that his son, who had been a captive, had been freed by Allah from their hands, and he had acquired some goats. He came and mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Are they lawful for me, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes."

He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn al-Mundhir al-Thawri, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym, regarding ﴿He will make for him a way out﴾. He said: From every matter that becomes narrow for people.

He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, regarding ﴿He will make for him a way out﴾. He said: He knows that Allah, if He wills, withholds from him, and if He wills, gives to him. ﴿And provides for him from where he does not expect﴾: that is, from where he does not know.

He said: Mihran related to us, from Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArouba, from Qatada, regarding ﴿He will make for him a way out﴾. He said: From the doubtful matters and the anguish at death. ﴿And provides for him from where he does not expect﴾: from where he does not hope or anticipate.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And provides for him from where he does not expect﴾: he does not anticipate or hope.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾.

He, may He be exalted, means: whoever fears Allah in his affairs and entrusts them to Him, then He is sufficient for him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾.

This is a separate statement from His saying: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾. Its meaning is: Indeed, Allah accomplishes His command in every case, whether the servant relies upon Him or does not rely upon Him.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) also said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, regarding ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾: He is sufficient for him whether he relies upon Him or does not, except that the one who relies upon Him will have his misdeeds expiated and will be given a great reward.

Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, saying: Abu Muʿawiya related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, with something similar.

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Silt related to us, from Qays, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud), regarding ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾. He said: The one whose need has been fulfilled is not the one who relies (upon Allah). The superiority of the one who relies upon Him over the one who does not is that his misdeeds are expiated and he is given a great reward.

He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: Shutayr ibn Shakl and Masruq were sitting together. Shutayr said: "Either you relate what you have heard from Ibn Masʿud so that I may confirm it, or I relate it so that you may confirm it for me?" Masruq said: "No, rather you relate it and I will confirm it." He said: "I heard Ibn Masʿud say: The greatest verse in the Qur'an regarding tafwid [[As in the original; I have not found this noun or its verb in the lexicons, and it is perhaps a corruption of "tafwid," which is the committing of the whole matter to Allah, and this is the meaning understood from this statement of Ibn Masʿud.]] is: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾." Masruq said: "You have spoken truly."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah has already set for everything a extent﴾.

He, may He be exalted, means: Allah has already set for everything, from divorce, the waiting period, and other matters, a limit, a term, and a measure at which it ends.

The people of ta'wil also said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Muʿawiya related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, regarding ﴿Allah has already set for everything a measure﴾. He said: A term.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, regarding ﴿Allah has already set for everything a measure﴾. He said: An endpoint.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, the same.

Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah has already set for everything a measure﴾. He said: The menstruation, in terms of the term and the waiting period.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 65, verse 4:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months, and those who have not menstruated [likewise]. And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden. And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him of his affair ease.﴾ (4)

He, exalted is He, says: And the women whose hope of menstruation has ceased, so that they no longer expect to menstruate, from among your women, if you are in doubt.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of His words ﴿if you are in doubt﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: if you are in doubt concerning the blood that appears from her due to her old age – whether it is from menstruation or from istihadah (irregular bleeding) – then their waiting period is three months.

Mention of those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿if you are in doubt﴾: if you do not know the one who has ceased menstruating, and the one who has not menstruated, then their waiting period is three months.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, regarding ﴿if you are in doubt﴾, he said: concerning her old age, that it may be due to old age; then she observes the waiting period of three months from the time she becomes doubtful. As for when a woman's menstruation ceases while she is young, one waits with her until it is seen whether she is pregnant or not. If her pregnancy becomes evident, her term is until she delivers her burden; and if her pregnancy does not become evident, then one waits until it becomes evident about her, and the furthest limit of that is a year.

- Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months﴾: if you doubt that she will not menstruate while her menstruation has ceased, or the men doubt, or she herself says: menstruation has left me, then their waiting period is three months if one doubts. Had she been pregnant, she would wait for the pregnancy until nine months had passed. He (the husband) feared and doubted, and so did she, that the menstruation had ended; it is not fitting for a Muslim woman to be held back, so she observes three months. Allah, exalted is His praise, also made it three months for the one who has not yet menstruated, the young girl.

- Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'bad informed us, saying: Sulayman was asked about the doubtful woman. He said: she is the doubtful woman who has ceased bearing children, who is divorced, then menstruates once, then at the time of her second menstruation she does not menstruate. He said: she observes, from the time she becomes doubtful, a waiting period of three months, beginning anew. He said: if she menstruates twice and then the time of the third arrives and she does not menstruate, she observes from the time she becomes doubtful a waiting period of three months, beginning anew, and does not count what has passed.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: if you are in doubt about their ruling, so that you do not know what the ruling concerning their waiting period is, then their waiting period is three months.

Mention of those who said this:

- Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Mutarrif informed us, from Amr ibn Salim, who said: "Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: O Messenger of Allah, a number of the categories of women are not mentioned in the Book: the young and the old, and those with burdens (pregnant women). So Allah revealed: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months, and those who have not menstruated, and for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden.﴾"

Others said: the meaning of that is: if you are in doubt about what appears from them of blood, so that you do not know whether it is blood of menstruation or blood of istihadah, whether that is due to old age or to an illness?

Mention of those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, who said: Among doubtful cases is the woman with istihadah, and the one whose menstruation is not regular, who menstruates several times in a month and once in several months; her waiting period is three months. This is the saying of Qatadah.

The most correct of these sayings is the saying of the one who said: what is intended is: if you are in doubt and do not know the ruling concerning them. This is because, if the meaning were as the one who said "if you are in doubt about their blood, not knowing whether it is menstrual blood or istihadah" had said, it would have been said: "if they are in doubt," for when the blood becomes unclear to them, it is they who are in doubt about their own blood and no one else's. The address in His words ﴿if you are in doubt﴾ to the men, and not to the women, is clear evidence for the correctness of what we have said, that its meaning is: if you men are in doubt about the ruling concerning them. Another point is that He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt﴾, and the one who has despaired of menstruation is the one who no longer hopes to menstruate due to old age. It is impossible to say: "those who have despaired" and then say: "if you doubt their despair," because despair is the cessation of hope, and doubting her despair implies hope for her, and it is not permissible for hope to be absent and present at the same time. Since the correct view is what we have said, it is clear that the interpretation of the verse is: those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt about the ruling concerning them and their waiting period, so that you do not know their status; the ruling on their waiting period, if they are divorced after consummation by their husbands, is three months. ﴿And those who have not menstruated﴾ means: likewise the waiting period of the young girls who have not menstruated, if their husbands divorce them after consummation.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

- Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation﴾, he said: the one whose menstruation has ceased, so her waiting period is three months. ﴿And those who have not menstruated﴾: he said: the young girls.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation﴾: they are those who have ceased menstruating and no longer menstruate. ﴿And those who have not menstruated﴾ are the virgins who have not menstruated; their waiting period is three months.

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation﴾ ... the verse, he said: the women who sit (qawa'id) from among women. ﴿And those who have not menstruated﴾: those who have not reached menstruation, and who have been touched (consummated); their waiting period is three months.

* *

And His words: ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾

Concerning the completion of their waiting period: that they deliver their burden. This is a consensus of all the scholars regarding a divorced pregnant woman. As for the widow, there is disagreement among the scholars.

We have mentioned their disagreement earlier in this book, and we will mention in this place some of what we did not mention there.

Mention of those who said: the ruling of His words ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾ is general, covering divorced women and widows.

- Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Ibn Shubrumah al-Kufi narrated to me, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Qays, that Ibn Mas'ud said: whoever wishes, I will curse him (in mubahalah), that the verse ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾ was not revealed except after the verse concerning the widow whose husband has died; and when the widow delivers, she is free. By the verse concerning the widow he means ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives, they shall wait by themselves four months and ten days﴾.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Malik, that is Ibn Isma'il, narrated to us, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Atiyyah, who said: I heard Ibn Mas'ud say: whoever wishes, I will dispute with him: the surah of al-Nisa al-Qusra (the shorter one) was revealed after it, meaning after four months and ten days.

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub informed us, from Muhammad, who said: I met Abu Atiyyah Malik ibn Amir and asked him about that, meaning about the widow whose husband has died if she delivers before the four months and ten days. He began to tell me the hadith of Subay'ah. I said: "No, have you heard anything from Abdullah about that?" He said: Yes, one day or one night it was mentioned to Abdullah, and he said: "Do you see that if four months and ten days pass and she has not delivered, has she become free?" They said: "No." He said: "Do you impose on her the strict ruling and do not grant her the concession? By Allah, the shorter women's surah was revealed after the longer one."

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, who said: al-Sha'bi said: whoever wishes, I will swear with him that the shorter women's verses were revealed after the four months and ten days mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah.

- Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud mentioned the later of the two terms, and said: whoever wishes, I will swear to him by Allah that this verse which was revealed concerning the shorter women was revealed after the four months, and then he said: the term of the pregnant woman is that she deliver what is in her womb.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, who said: I said to al-Sha'bi: I do not believe that Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: the later of the two terms is that a widow whose husband has died may not marry until the later of the two terms has passed. Al-Sha'bi said: Yes, and he spoke the truth, the most truthful thing I have ever heard. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: His words ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾ refer only to divorced women. Then he said: Ali and Abdullah used to say concerning divorce that her term is fulfilled when she delivers her burden.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾, I said: O Messenger of Allah, the widow whose husband has died and the divorced woman? He said: "Yes."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Mukhariq, who narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾, and he said: The term of every pregnant woman is that she deliver what is in her womb."

- Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾: he said: for the pregnant woman whom her husband divorces while she is pregnant, her waiting period is that she deliver her burden.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾: when she delivers what is in her womb, her waiting period has ended; menstruation has nothing to do with her affair when she is pregnant.

Others said: that is specific to divorced women, and as for the widow, her waiting period is the later of the two terms; this is a view reported from Ali and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.

We have mentioned the narration to this effect from them earlier.

The correct view on this matter is that it is general, covering divorced women and widows, because Allah, mighty and majestic, made it general by His words ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾, and did not restrict this statement to a divorced woman rather than a widow; rather, the statement covers all pregnant women. If someone supposes that His words ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾ occur in the context of rulings about divorced women and not widows, then the ruling about divorced women is more appropriate for them than the ruling about widows; but the matter is not as he supposed. That is because, although it occurs in the context of rulings about divorced women, it is separate from the rulings about divorced women; rather, it is a new statement about the waiting period of all pregnant women, divorced and non-divorced, and there is no indication from report or reason that it is meant for some pregnant women rather than others. So it is general, as we have explained.

* *

And His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him of his affair ease﴾

He, mighty is His praise, says: whoever fears Allah and is wary of Him, avoids His disobediences, performs His obligations, and does not oppose His permission regarding the divorce of his wife, then Allah will make for him, from that divorce, ease: that it will be easy for him, if he desires the concession by following his own desire, to take her back while she is in her waiting period; and if her waiting period has ended and then his soul moves him toward her, he will be able to propose to her.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 65, verse 5:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿That is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you. And whoever fears Allah, He will remove from him his misdeeds and will magnify for him a reward﴾

He, the Exalted, says: This that I have made clear to you of the rulings concerning divorce, return (al-raj'ah), and the waiting period (al-'iddah) is the command of Allah which He has commanded you with, which He has sent down to you, O people, so that you may comply with it and act upon it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will remove from him his misdeeds﴾

He says: And whoever fears Allah, safeguarding himself by avoiding His disobedience and performing His obligations, Allah will erase from him his sins and the misdeeds of his deeds. ﴿And will magnify for him a reward﴾ means: and will bestow abundant reward upon him for that deed and his taqwa (God-consciousness). And among the magnifying of the reward for him is that He will admit him into His Paradise, granting him eternal abiding therein.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means﴾ — He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Lodge the women you have divorced in the place where you dwell, ﴿according to your means﴾, meaning: according to your ample means that you find; and He only commanded the men to give them a dwelling in which they may reside, from what they are able to afford, until they complete their waiting periods (ʿiddah).

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means﴾, he said: according to your ample means.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿according to your means﴾, he said: according to your ampleness.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means﴾, he said: according to your ampleness.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, regarding His saying: ﴿Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means, and do not harm them so as to constrict them﴾: if you find nothing but a corner of your house, then lodge her in it.

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means﴾, he said: concerning a woman whom her husband divorces, it is incumbent upon him to lodge her and to provide for her.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means﴾, and he said: according to your capacity, wherever you are able. If you have nothing, and you were residing in a dwelling that is not yours, and then a command came that removed you from the dwelling, and you have no dwelling to reside in, and you do not find one, then that is the case; and if he has the strength to rent, then that is his means, and he does not remove her from her home. And if he does not find, and the owner of the dwelling says: I will not lodge her in my house, then it is so; and if he is able, then that is incumbent upon him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and do not harm them so as to constrict them﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: do not harm them in the dwelling in which you lodge them, while you find ample dwellings, by seeking to constrict them; this is His saying: ﴿so as to constrict them﴾, meaning: so that you constrict them in the dwelling while you have ampleness.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and do not harm them so as to constrict them﴾, he said: in the dwelling.

• Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿according to your means﴾, he said: according to your possession, according to your capacity.

And regarding His saying: ﴿and do not harm them so as to constrict them﴾, he said: so that you constrict their dwellings for them until they leave.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿and do not harm them so as to constrict them﴾, he said: it is not proper for him to harm her and constrict her in her place. ﴿until they lay down their burden﴾: this applies to the one who holds the right of return and to the one who does not hold the right of return.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them until they lay down their burden﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: if your divorced women are pregnant, and they are irrevocably separated from you, then spend upon them during their waiting period from you until they lay down their burden.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them until they lay down their burden﴾: this is the woman whose husband divorces her, and her divorce is final while she is pregnant; Allah commands him to lodge her and to spend upon her until she gives birth; and if she nurses, then until she is weaned. And if he has irrevocably divorced her and she is not pregnant, then she has the right to lodging until her waiting period ends, with no maintenance. Likewise the woman whose husband dies and leaves her: if she is pregnant, he spends upon her from the share of the one in her womb, if there is an inheritance; and if there is no inheritance, the heir spends upon her until she gives birth and weans her child, as Allah, mighty and majestic is He, said: ﴿and upon the heir is the like of that﴾. But if she is not pregnant, her maintenance is from her own property.

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them until they lay down their burden﴾, he said: one spends upon the pregnant woman while she is pregnant, until she lays down her burden.

Others said: what is meant by His saying: ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them until they lay down their burden﴾ is every divorced woman, whether her husband holds the right of return to her or not.

Among those who said this were ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab and ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Mention of the transmission from them to that effect:

• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, who said: ʿUmar and ʿAbd Allah used to assign to the woman divorced three times: lodging, maintenance, and consolation gift (mutʿah). And when ʿUmar was told of the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays, that the Prophet ﷺ commanded her to observe her waiting period outside her husband's house, he said: We would not permit in our religion the testimony of a woman.

• Nasr ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from ʿIsa ibn Qirtas, who said: I heard ʿAli ibn al-Husayn say regarding the woman divorced three times: she has lodging, maintenance, and consolation gift; but if she leaves her house, then she has no lodging, no maintenance, and no consolation gift.

• Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbuʿi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, who said: for the woman divorced three times: lodging and maintenance.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: if a man divorces three times, she has lodging and maintenance.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that there is no maintenance for the irrevocably divorced woman unless she is pregnant, because Allah, mighty and majestic is He, made maintenance by His saying: (And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them) for pregnant women, to the exclusion of other irrevocably divorced women from their husbands. And if the irrevocably divorced pregnant and non-pregnant women were equal in what is owed to them of maintenance from their husbands, there would be no intelligible reason for singling out those who are pregnant in this place, since they and the others would be equal in that; and in their being singled out to the exclusion of others lies the strongest proof that there is no maintenance for the irrevocably divorced woman unless she is pregnant.

And in accordance with what we have said in this matter, the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is authentic.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn Bakr narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, who said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, saying: Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: Fatimah bint Qays, sister of al-Dahhak ibn Qays, told me that Abu ʿAmr al-Makhzumi divorced her three times, and he ordered maintenance for her, but she considered it little. Now the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent him toward Yemen, so Khalid ibn al-Walid went with a group of the Banu Makhzum to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was at the house of Maymunah, and said: O Messenger of Allah, Abu ʿAmr divorced Fatimah three times; does she have any maintenance? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "She has no maintenance." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to her: move to the house of Umm Sharik, and he sent to her: do not outrun me with yourself; then he sent to her that the early emigrants visit Umm Sharik, so move to Ibn Umm Maktum, for when you remove your veil, he will not see you. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her to Usamah ibn Zayd.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And if they nurse for you, then give them their wages﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: if your women who are irrevocably divorced from you nurse your young children for you for a wage, then give them their wages for their nursing of them.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, that he said regarding nursing: if she stands upon a price, the child's mother has more right to it; if she wishes she nurses him, and if she wishes she leaves him, unless he does not accept from anyone else; and if that is the case, she is compelled to nurse him.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And if they nurse for you, then give them their wages﴾: she has more right to her child, to take him at what you had been paying another to nurse him.

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And if they nurse for you, then give them their wages﴾, he said: what they agree upon.

﴿According to the wealthy his means, and according to the straitened his means﴾.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, concerning the child who stands upon a price: his mother has more right to nurse him; if no one is found to nurse him, the mother is compelled to nurse.

• He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿then give them their wages﴾, he said: if she nurses for you for a higher wage, she has more right than others; and if she refuses to nurse him and does not agree with you on what is between you and her, and you disagree about the wage, then hire another woman to nurse him for him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And let you consult together in kindness﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: let some of you, O people, accept from one another what you enjoin upon one another of what is right.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿And let you consult together in kindness﴾, he said: do what is good among yourselves.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿And let you consult together in kindness﴾: urging one another.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And if you disagree, then another woman will nurse for him﴾

He says: if the man and the woman disagree over the nursing of their child by him, and she refuses to nurse him, then he has no authority over her, and he has no right to compel her to nurse him; but he hires a wet-nurse for the child other than his divorced mother.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:
