• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿And if you disagree, then another woman will nurse for him﴾, he said: if the mother refuses to nurse her child when his father has divorced her, he seeks another wet-nurse for him; the mother has more right, if she is content, to the wage for nursing at what another would be content with, so he should not take him from her.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: if she refuses to nurse him and does not agree with you between her and you, and you disagree about the wage, then hire another woman to nurse him for him.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿And if you disagree, then another woman will nurse for him. Let the wealthy spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾, he said: he imposed upon her according to what she finds; she said: I am not content with this; he said: this is after separation, but while she is his wife, she nurses for him willingly or unwillingly, if she wishes, and if she refuses. So he said to her: I have no more than this; if you wish to nurse at this, then nurse; and if you dislike it, then he hires someone to nurse my child. This is His saying: ﴿And if you disagree, then another woman will nurse for him﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: let the one whose wife has been irrevocably separated from him, if he is wealthy in property and rich by the ampleness of his wealth, spend upon his irrevocably divorced wife for the wage of nursing his child by her, and upon his young child. ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted﴾: that is, whoever has his provision constricted for him and is not given abundance, let him spend from what Allah has given him, according to the measure of his property and what he has been given of it.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth﴾, he said: from the ampleness of his possessor. He said: ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted﴾, he said: whose provision is constricted for him.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth﴾, meaning: from his capacity.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾, he said: he imposed upon her according to what he finds.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to me, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth﴾, he said: upon the divorced woman when she nurses for him.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about Abu ʿUbaydah, and it was said to him: he wears coarse garments and eats the roughest food. So he sent him a thousand dinars and said to the messenger: watch what he does when he takes them. He did not wait long before he wore the softest garments and ate the finest food. The messenger came and informed him, and he said, may Allah have mercy on him: he interpreted this verse: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾

He says: Allah does not burden anyone with spending upon those whose maintenance is obligatory for him by kinship and kinship ties, except what He has given him: if he is wealthy, then from his wealth; and if his provision is restricted, then from what Allah has provided him, according to his capacity. He does not burden the poor with the spending of the rich, nor any of His creatures except the obligation He has imposed upon him.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾, he said: He says: He does not burden the poor with what He burdens the rich.

• ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hushaym: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾, he said: except what He has enjoined upon it.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾, he said: except what it is able to bear.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾, he said: Allah does not burden him to give charity when he has nothing to give in charity, nor does Allah burden him to pay zakah when he has nothing with which to pay zakah.

And His saying: ﴿and do not harm them so as to constrict them﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: do not harm them in the dwelling in which you lodge them, while you find ample dwellings, by seeking to constrict them; this is His saying: ﴿so as to constrict them﴾, meaning: so that you constrict them in the dwelling while you have ampleness.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and do not harm them so as to constrict them﴾, he said: in the dwelling.

• Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿according to your means﴾, he said: according to your possession, according to your capacity.

And regarding His saying: ﴿and do not harm them so as to constrict them﴾, he said: so that you constrict their dwellings for them until they leave.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿and do not harm them so as to constrict them﴾, he said: it is not proper for him to harm her and constrict her in her place. ﴿until they lay down their burden﴾: this applies to the one who holds the right of return and to the one who does not hold the right of return.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them until they lay down their burden﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: if your divorced women are pregnant, and they are irrevocably separated from you, then spend upon them during their waiting period from you until they lay down their burden.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them until they lay down their burden﴾: this is the woman whose husband divorces her, and her divorce is final while she is pregnant; Allah commands him to lodge her and to spend upon her until she gives birth; and if she nurses, then until she is weaned. And if he has irrevocably divorced her and she is not pregnant, then she has the right to lodging until her waiting period ends, with no maintenance. Likewise the woman whose husband dies and leaves her: if she is pregnant, he spends upon her from the share of the one in her womb, if there is an inheritance; and if there is no inheritance, the heir spends upon her until she gives birth and weans her child, as Allah, mighty and majestic is He, said: ﴿and upon the heir is the like of that﴾. But if she is not pregnant, her maintenance is from her own property.

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them until they lay down their burden﴾, he said: one spends upon the pregnant woman while she is pregnant, until she lays down her burden.

Others said: what is meant by His saying: ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them until they lay down their burden﴾ is every divorced woman, whether her husband holds the right of return to her or not.

Among those who said this were ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab and ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Mention of the transmission from them to that effect:

• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, who said: ʿUmar and ʿAbd Allah used to assign to the woman divorced three times: lodging, maintenance, and consolation gift (mutʿah). And when ʿUmar was told of the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays, that the Prophet ﷺ commanded her to observe her waiting period outside her husband's house, he said: We would not permit in our religion the testimony of a woman.

• Nasr ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from ʿIsa ibn Qirtas, who said: I heard ʿAli ibn al-Husayn say regarding the woman divorced three times: she has lodging, maintenance, and consolation gift; but if she leaves her house, then she has no lodging, no maintenance, and no consolation gift.

• Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbuʿi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, who said: for the woman divorced three times: lodging and maintenance.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: if a man divorces three times, she has lodging and maintenance.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that there is no maintenance for the irrevocably divorced woman unless she is pregnant, because Allah, mighty and majestic is He, made maintenance by His saying: (And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them) for pregnant women, to the exclusion of other irrevocably divorced women from their husbands. And if the irrevocably divorced pregnant and non-pregnant women were equal in what is owed to them of maintenance from their husbands, there would be no intelligible reason for singling out those who are pregnant in this place, since they and the others would be equal in that; and in their being singled out to the exclusion of others lies the strongest proof that there is no maintenance for the irrevocably divorced woman unless she is pregnant.

And in accordance with what we have said in this matter, the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is authentic.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn Bakr narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, who said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, saying: Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: Fatimah bint Qays, sister of al-Dahhak ibn Qays, told me that Abu ʿAmr al-Makhzumi divorced her three times, and he ordered maintenance for her, but she considered it little. Now the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent him toward Yemen, so Khalid ibn al-Walid went with a group of the Banu Makhzum to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was at the house of Maymunah, and said: O Messenger of Allah, Abu ʿAmr divorced Fatimah three times; does she have any maintenance? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "She has no maintenance." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to her: move to the house of Umm Sharik, and he sent to her: do not outrun me with yourself; then he sent to her that the early emigrants visit Umm Sharik, so move to Ibn Umm Maktum, for when you remove your veil, he will not see you. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her to Usamah ibn Zayd.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And if they nurse for you, then give them their wages﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: if your women who are irrevocably divorced from you nurse your young children for you for a wage, then give them their wages for their nursing of them.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, that he said regarding nursing: if she stands upon a price, the child's mother has more right to it; if she wishes she nurses him, and if she wishes she leaves him, unless he does not accept from anyone else; and if that is the case, she is compelled to nurse him.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And if they nurse for you, then give them their wages﴾: she has more right to her child, to take him at what you had been paying another to nurse him.

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And if they nurse for you, then give them their wages﴾, he said: what they agree upon.

﴿According to the wealthy his means, and according to the straitened his means﴾.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, concerning the child who stands upon a price: his mother has more right to nurse him; if no one is found to nurse him, the mother is compelled to nurse.

• He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿then give them their wages﴾, he said: if she nurses for you for a higher wage, she has more right than others; and if she refuses to nurse him and does not agree with you on what is between you and her, and you disagree about the wage, then hire another woman to nurse him for him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And let you consult together in kindness﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: let some of you, O people, accept from one another what you enjoin upon one another of what is right.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿And let you consult together in kindness﴾, he said: do what is good among yourselves.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿And let you consult together in kindness﴾: urging one another.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And if you disagree, then another woman will nurse for him﴾

He says: if the man and the woman disagree over the nursing of their child by him, and she refuses to nurse him, then he has no authority over her, and he has no right to compel her to nurse him; but he hires a wet-nurse for the child other than his divorced mother.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿And if you disagree, then another woman will nurse for him﴾, he said: if the mother refuses to nurse her child when his father has divorced her, he seeks another wet-nurse for him; the mother has more right, if she is content, to the wage for nursing at what another would be content with, so he should not take him from her.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: if she refuses to nurse him and does not agree with you between her and you, and you disagree about the wage, then hire another woman to nurse him for him.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿And if you disagree, then another woman will nurse for him. Let the wealthy spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾, he said: he imposed upon her according to what she finds; she said: I am not content with this; he said: this is after separation, but while she is his wife, she nurses for him willingly or unwillingly, if she wishes, and if she refuses. So he said to her: I have no more than this; if you wish to nurse at this, then nurse; and if you dislike it, then he hires someone to nurse my child. This is His saying: ﴿And if you disagree, then another woman will nurse for him﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: let the one whose wife has been irrevocably separated from him, if he is wealthy in property and rich by the ampleness of his wealth, spend upon his irrevocably divorced wife for the wage of nursing his child by her, and upon his young child. ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted﴾: that is, whoever has his provision constricted for him and is not given abundance, let him spend from what Allah has given him, according to the measure of his property and what he has been given of it.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth﴾, he said: from the ampleness of his possessor. He said: ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted﴾, he said: whose provision is constricted for him.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth﴾, meaning: from his capacity.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾, he said: he imposed upon her according to what he finds.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to me, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth﴾, he said: upon the divorced woman when she nurses for him.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about Abu ʿUbaydah, and it was said to him: he wears coarse garments and eats the roughest food. So he sent him a thousand dinars and said to the messenger: watch what he does when he takes them. He did not wait long before he wore the softest garments and ate the finest food. The messenger came and informed him, and he said, may Allah have mercy on him: he interpreted this verse: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾

He says: Allah does not burden anyone with spending upon those whose maintenance is obligatory for him by kinship and kinship ties, except what He has given him: if he is wealthy, then from his wealth; and if his provision is restricted, then from what Allah has provided him, according to his capacity. He does not burden the poor with the spending of the rich, nor any of His creatures except the obligation He has imposed upon him.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾, he said: He says: He does not burden the poor with what He burdens the rich.

• ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hushaym: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾, he said: except what He has enjoined upon it.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾, he said: except what it is able to bear.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾, he said: Allah does not burden him to give charity when he has nothing to give in charity, nor does Allah burden him to pay zakah when he has nothing with which to pay zakah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 65, verses 8–9:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We called it to a severe account and punished it with a terrible punishment. So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair, and the outcome of its affair was loss.﴾

His words, exalted is He, mean: ﴿Allah will bring about﴾ for the one of restricted means whose provision is limited, ﴿after hardship, ease﴾. He says: after severity, relief; after narrowness, abundance; after poverty, wealth.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿Allah will bring about after hardship, ease﴾: after severity, relief.

* *

And His words: ﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers﴾

He, exalted is He, means: how many a people of a town transgressed against the command of their Lord and opposed Him, and against the command of their Lord's messengers, persisting in their transgression and obstinacy, and persisting in their disbelief.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers﴾, he said: it altered and disobeyed.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We called it to a severe account﴾, he said: the transgression (utuw) here is disbelief and disobedience; "ataw" means disbelief; "rebelled against the command of its Lord" means it abandoned it and did not accept it.

It was also said: they were a people who opposed the command of their Lord regarding divorce, so Allah, by informing about them, threatened this community that He would do to them what He did to those [people] if they opposed His command in that matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, saying: I heard Umar ibn Sulayman say regarding His words: ﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers﴾, he said: a town that was punished over divorce.

* *

And His words: ﴿So We called it to a severe account﴾

He says: We called it to account for Our blessings upon it and its gratitude, a severe account; that is, an account in which We were thorough with them, not pardoning them in anything, nor overlooking anything for them.

As:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿So We called it to a severe account﴾, he said: We did not pardon it; the severe account in which there is no pardon at all.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿So We called it to a severe account﴾, he said: We showed no mercy.

* *

And His words: ﴿And We punished it with a terrible punishment﴾

He says: We punished it with a great and dreadful punishment, and that punishment is the punishment of Hell.

* *

And His words: ﴿So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair﴾

He says: this town that rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers tasted the consequence of what it did and committed of disobedience to Allah and disbelief in Him.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair﴾, he said: the punishment of its affair.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair﴾, he said: it tasted the consequence of the evil it did; al-wabal means the consequence.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair﴾, he said: the consequence of its affair.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair﴾, he said: the recompense of its affair.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair﴾, he said: meaning by the evil consequence of its affair: the recompense of its affair that has already befallen.

* *

And His words: ﴿And the outcome of its affair was loss﴾

He, exalted is He, says: and what resulted from their affair, which was their disbelief in Allah and their disobedience to Him, was loss; that is, deprivation, because they sold the bliss of the Hereafter for a meager, paltry worldly gain, and preferred following their desires over following the command of Allah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 65, verse 10:

Concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. So fear Allah, O people of understanding who have believed. Allah has indeed sent down to you a reminder, a Messenger reciting to you the clear signs of Allah﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Allah has prepared for these people, who transgressed against the command of their Lord and His messengers, a severe punishment, and that is the punishment of the Fire which He has prepared for them on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿So fear Allah, O people of understanding﴾: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: fear Allah, and beware of His wrath by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, O people of intellect.

As follows:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, who said: Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words: ﴿So fear Allah, O people of understanding﴾, he said: O people of intellect.

* *

And His saying: ﴿who have believed﴾

means: those who affirmed Allah and His messengers.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Allah has indeed sent down to you a reminder, a Messenger﴾

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning what is meant by the reminder and the Messenger in this place. Some of them said: the reminder is the Qur'an, and the Messenger is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, who said: Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words: ﴿Allah has indeed sent down to you a reminder, a Messenger﴾, he said: The reminder: the Qur'an, and the Messenger: Muhammad (ﷺ).

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the words of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Allah has indeed sent down to you a reminder﴾, he said: The Qur'an is a spirit from Allah, and he recited: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command﴾ to the end of the verse, and he recited: ﴿Allah has indeed sent down to you a reminder, a Messenger﴾, he said: the Qur'an. And he recited: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved in the reminder when it came to them﴾, he said: by the Qur'an. And he recited: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the reminder﴾, he said: the Qur'an. He said: it is the reminder, and it is the spirit.

Others said: the reminder is the Messenger.

The correct view on this matter is that "Messenger" is an explanatory apposition to "reminder"; it is in the accusative because it is governed by it, as an explanation and clarification of it.

So the meaning of the statement is: Allah has indeed sent down to you, O people of understanding, a reminder from Allah by which He reminds you and alerts you to your share of faith in Allah and acting in obedience to Him, a Messenger reciting to you the signs of Allah which He sent down to him, ﴿clear﴾: meaning clear to whoever hears them and reflects on them that they are from Allah.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That He may bring forth those who have believed and done righteous deeds from darknesses into light. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah has certainly perfected for him a provision﴾ [65:11].

Say: His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Allah has sent down to you, O people, a reminder, a Messenger reciting to you the clear verses of Allah, so that those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger may be brought out: ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, meaning: and acted upon what Allah commanded them and obeyed Him, ﴿from darknesses into light﴾, meaning from disbelief, which is darkness, into light, meaning into faith.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness﴾

Meaning: whoever affirms Allah and acts in obedience to Him, ﴿He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, meaning: He will admit him to orchards beneath whose trees rivers flow, ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, meaning: remaining and dwelling in the orchards beneath which rivers flow, forever; they will not die, nor will they ever leave them.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Allah has certainly perfected for him a provision﴾

Meaning: Allah has certainly made abundant for him in the gardens a provision. By provision is meant what He provides for him there of food and drink, and all else that He has prepared for His friends therein, which He has made good for them.

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿It is Allah who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof. The command descends among them so that you may know that Allah is over all things competent, and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge.﴾ (12)

His words, the Exalted, mean: It is Allah, not the idols and images that the polytheists worship, which have no power to create anything, who created seven heavens.

And His words: ﴿and of the earth the like thereof﴾

That is: He created from the earth the like of them, for in each of them is the like of the creation that is in the heavens.

Those who said this:

Amr ibn Ali and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn Abbas, who said concerning this verse: ﴿It is Allah who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾. Amr said: He said: In every earth [there is] a [creature like] Ibrahim, and [there is] something similar to the creation that is on the earth. And Ibn al-Muthanna said: In every heaven [there is] an Ibrahim.

Amr ibn Ali related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, saying: al-A'mash related to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿It is Allah who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾. He said: If I were to tell you its interpretation, you would disbelieve, and your disbelief would be your denial of it.

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Abu Bakr related to us, from Asim, from Zirr, from Abdullah, who said: Allah created seven heavens, the thickness of each being a five-hundred-year journey, and between each one and the next is five hundred years. Above the seven heavens is water, and Allah, may His praise be exalted, is above the water; nothing of the deeds of the children of Adam is hidden from Him. The earths are seven, between each earth and the next is five hundred years, and the thickness of each earth is five hundred years.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'd al-Qummi al-Ash'ari related to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah al-Khuza'i, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man said to Ibn Abbas: ﴿It is Allah who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾ ... the verse. Ibn Abbas said: What assures you that I will tell you of it and you will not disbelieve?

He said: Abbas related to us, from Anbasah, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: This earth in relation to that one is like a tent pitched in a desert, and this heaven in relation to that heaven is like a ring thrown into a desert land.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: The first heaven is a restrained wave; the second is rock; the third is iron; the fourth is copper; the fifth is silver; the sixth is gold; and the seventh is a ruby.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim related to us, saying: Humayd ibn Qays related to me, from Mujahid, who said: This House, the Ka'bah, is the fourth of fourteen houses, one in each heaven, each house directly opposite the next; if it fell, it would fall upon it. And this sanctuary, my sanctuary, was built from the seven heavens and the seven earths.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿It is Allah who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾: He created seven heavens and seven earths, in each of His heavens and each of His earths, a creation from His creatures, a command from His command, and a decree from His decree.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: While the Prophet ﷺ was sitting once with his Companions, a cloud passed by. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do you know what this is? This is the clouds; these are the water-skins of the earth, which Allah drives to a people who do not worship Him." He said: "Do you know what this sky is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "This sky is a restrained wave and a preserved roof." Then he said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Above that is another sky," and he kept counting until he had counted seven heavens, saying: "Do you know what is between them?" "Five hundred years." Then he said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Above that is the Throne." He said: "Do you know what is between them?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Between them is five hundred years." Then he said: "Do you know what this earth is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Beneath that is an earth." He said: "Do you know how far between them is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Between them is a journey of five hundred years," until he counted seven earths. Then he said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, if a man were lowered on a rope until he reached the lowest of the seventh earths, he would descend upon Allah." Then he recited: ﴿He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward, and He is Knower of all things﴾.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "Four angels met between the sky and the earth. One said to the others: 'Where have you come from?' One of them said: 'My Lord sent me from the seventh heaven, and I left Him there.' Then another said: 'My Lord sent me from the seventh earth, and I left Him there.' Then another said: 'My Lord sent me from the east, and I left Him there.' Then another said: 'My Lord sent me from the west, and I left Him there.'"

* *

His words: ﴿The command descends among them﴾

That is: the command of Allah descends between the seventh heaven and the seventh earth.

As related:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿The command descends among them﴾: between the seventh earth and the seventh heaven.

* *

His words: ﴿so that you may know that Allah is over all things competent﴾

That is: the decree and command of Allah descends between these, so that you, O people, may know the reality of His power and authority, and that nothing He wills is beyond His capacity, and no matter He intends is out of His reach; rather, He is competent over whatever He wills. ﴿And that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾: that is, His majesty says: so that you, O people, may know that Allah encompasses every thing of His creation in knowledge, and not even the weight of an atom in the earth or in the heaven escapes Him, nor anything smaller or larger than that. His majesty says: so beware, O people who oppose the command of your Lord, of His punishment, for nothing prevents Him from punishing you, and He is capable of that; and He also encompasses your deeds, so nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He counts them against you, to repay you for them, on the day when every soul will be repaid for what it earned.

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Talaq.
